The AI computing boom — requiring massive quantities of GPU-accelerated compute — has further accelerated Texas data center investment. NVIDIA and other semiconductor companies have established significant Texas presences. Texas has positioned itself as a hub for tech sector migration from California, with companies including Tesla, Oracle, and HP Enterprise having moved headquarters. The data center boom strains the electricity grid and raises water usage concerns in a drought-prone state.
laws.penalty: Data centers must comply with environmental permits and water use regulations; tech companies face various state business requirements
exceptions: Qualifying projects may receive property tax abatements under Chapter 313 programs or successors

quiz.q: Which factor has NOT been a major driver of Texas's data center boom?
options: World's largest fiber optic network capacity
quiz.explanation: Texas's data center boom has been driven by available land, business-friendly regulation, relatively cheap electricity, and tax incentives — not a uniquely large fiber network. Texas competes for data center investment against Virginia, which actually leads in US data center density.

laws.title: Immigration Border Enforcement and State-Federal Conflict
laws.subtitle: Texas pursuing its own border policy separate from federal government
laws.fullDescription: Texas has pursued one of the most aggressive state-level immigration enforcement efforts in US history, with Governor Greg Abbott's Operation Lone Star deploying Texas National Guard troops and law enforcement to the border. Texas attempted to install floating barriers in the Rio Grande, argued to be unlawful by federal courts. Texas passed SB4, which criminalized illegal border crossing under state law and allowed Texas police to arrest and deport migrants — a law challenged in federal court and enjoined by judges who ruled immigration enforcement was exclusively federal. Texas has bused migrants to Democratic cities (Chicago, New York, Washington) as a political statement. The state has been in open conflict with the Biden administration over border authority, and the Supreme Court resolved some aspects of the dispute. Texas's experiences illustrate fundamental constitutional questions about immigration federalism.
laws.penalty: SB4 criminal provisions (when enforceable) carry misdemeanor and felony charges; migrant transportation operations face federal scrutiny
exceptions: Asylum seekers have specific legal protections under federal law that state enforcement cannot override
laws.sourceLabel: Texas Office of the Governor Border Security

quiz.q: What did Texas's SB4 law attempt to do regarding immigration enforcement?
options: Create a state guest worker program
Criminalize illegal border crossing under state law and allow Texas police to arrest migrants
Penalize businesses that hire undocumented workers
Require proof of citizenship for voting and government services
quiz.explanation: Texas's SB4 attempted to criminalize illegal border crossing under state law and allow Texas police to arrest and deport migrants — a power federal courts ruled belonged exclusively to the federal government under the US Constitution.

laws.title: Hurricane Beryl Grid Failure
laws.subtitle: Texas power grid fails again in 2024 summer storm
laws.fullDescription: Hurricane Beryl made landfall in Texas in July 2024 as a Category 1 storm but caused widespread, prolonged power outages affecting millions in the Houston area. The outages lasted weeks for some customers in record summer heat, causing deaths. The Texas power grid (ERCOT) faced renewed criticism for its vulnerability. The failures echoed the deadly Winter Storm Uri of 2021. Texas legislators debated mandatory weatherization requirements and grid interconnection with the broader US grid, though strong opposition to federal oversight remained.
laws.penalty: ERCOT and utilities face regulatory penalties for extended outages; weatherization standards required for generators after Winter Storm Uri
exceptions: Weatherization requirements apply to power generators; residential compliance voluntary
Small rural cooperatives have phased compliance timelines

quiz.q: What weather event exposed Texas's power grid vulnerabilities in July 2024, similar to Winter Storm Uri in 2021?
quiz.explanation: Hurricane Beryl made landfall in Texas in July 2024 and caused prolonged, deadly power outages in Houston, renewing criticism of ERCOT and the Texas power grid's vulnerability that had first gained national attention during Winter Storm Uri in 2021.

laws.title: ERCOT AI Grid Management
laws.subtitle: Texas uses machine learning to manage world's largest independent grid
laws.fullDescription: Texas's ERCOT grid, the nation's largest independent grid serving 90% of Texas, has deployed AI and machine learning tools to better predict renewable energy generation, forecast demand and optimize power dispatch. The grid's famous volatility—from Winter Storm Uri to Summer heat waves—has accelerated adoption of predictive analytics. AI tools help ERCOT balance the world's largest wind generation capacity with demand. However the grid remains isolated from neighboring grids and thus vulnerable to extreme weather events.
laws.penalty: ERCOT operates under PUC of Texas oversight; grid reliability standards subject to regulatory review
exceptions: Transmission companies operate under FERC jurisdiction for interstate connections
Retail electricity providers regulated separately from generation and transmission

quiz.q: What percentage of Texas does the ERCOT grid serve?
quiz.explanation: ERCOT serves approximately 90% of Texas, making it the nation's largest independent grid—intentionally isolated from neighboring grids to avoid FERC federal oversight, which also leaves it uniquely vulnerable to extreme weather events.

laws.title: Population Boom and Housing Development
laws.subtitle: Texas adds more residents than any other state
laws.fullDescription: Texas has been the fastest-growing state for several years, with cities like Austin, Dallas-Fort Worth, Houston and San Antonio adding hundreds of thousands of residents annually. Unlike California, Texas has relatively permissive zoning laws and land availability enabling significant housing construction. Despite this, Austin's housing prices roughly doubled in the post-COVID period before partially correcting. Texas's growth reflects migration from high-cost states, job creation and relative affordability—though affordability is declining in major metros.
laws.penalty: Property taxes fund local government; no state income tax creates reliance on property tax that rises with home values
exceptions: Homestead exemptions reduce property tax burden for primary residences
Property tax caps limit annual assessment increases for homesteads

quiz.q: How does Texas primarily fund local government instead of using a state income tax?
quiz.explanation: Texas funds local government primarily through property taxes because it has no state income tax—a trade-off that keeps income taxes low but means property taxes rise significantly as home values increase during Texas's population boom.

laws.title: Railroad Commission Methane Regulations
laws.subtitle: Oil and Gas Emissions in the Permian Basin
laws.fullDescription: The Texas Railroad Commission — which despite its name regulates oil and gas — oversees methane emissions from the massive Permian Basin oil and gas operations. Texas has been under pressure to strengthen its regulations as satellite data revealed significant methane leaks from Permian operations. The commission requires operators to report flaring events and has rules against routine flaring, though enforcement has been criticized as lax compared to federal EPA standards.
laws.penalty: Fines from $150 to $10,000 per day per violation; permit suspension for repeat offenders
exceptions: Emergency flaring during equipment failure
New well completion flaring under 10 days
Remote locations with no pipeline access

laws.title: Texas Maternal Mortality and Morbidity
laws.subtitle: Maternal Death Crisis in a Large State
laws.fullDescription: Texas has one of the highest maternal mortality rates in the developed world, particularly affecting Black women. The Texas Maternal Mortality and Morbidity Review Committee (MMMRC) was established by state law to review maternal deaths and make recommendations. Texas's 2021 near-total abortion ban (SB 8 and subsequent laws) has been linked by medical researchers to increased maternal deaths and dangerous delays in obstetric emergency care. Texas also has a high proportion of uninsured residents due to its refusal to expand Medicaid, affecting prenatal care access.
laws.penalty: Hospitals legally required to report maternal deaths; physician reporting mandated
exceptions: Physician determinations of medical necessity in emergency situations
Federal EMTALA requirements apply regardless of state law

laws.title: Texas Right-to-Work Law
laws.subtitle: Unions in the Lone Star State
laws.fullDescription: Texas is a right-to-work state under the National Labor Relations Act, meaning workers cannot be required to join a union or pay union dues as a condition of employment. Texas also has no state minimum wage law — defaulting to the federal $7.25/hour minimum. Texas prohibits local minimum wage ordinances, blocking cities like Austin and Dallas from setting higher minimums. Texas has one of the lowest unionization rates in the US (~5%). Despite being pro-business, Texas workers in the oil and gas industry — historically well-paid — have seen significant pay compression as the industry consolidated.
laws.penalty: NLRA: unfair labor practice charges for union membership coercion; wage violations: DOL enforcement
exceptions: Federal government workers under separate framework
Agricultural workers historically excluded from federal labor law

laws.title: Texas Top 10% Rule
laws.subtitle: Guaranteed UT Austin Admission
laws.fullDescription: Texas's Top 10% Rule (1997) guarantees admission to any Texas public university for students graduating in the top 10% of their Texas high school class, applying to the University of Texas at Austin. Created after affirmative action was banned in Texas by the 5th Circuit Hopwood decision, the rule was designed to maintain diversity through class-rank. It has been remarkably effective — providing access to Latino and Black students from high-poverty schools. Texas has since limited the automatic admission provision to the top 6% at UT Austin due to capacity. Texas also banned DEI offices in public universities in 2023.
laws.penalty: Universities must honor the guarantee; misrepresentation of class rank: revocation of admission; DEI violations: loss of state funding
exceptions: Top 6% automatic to UT Austin (reduced from 10%)
Graduate programs under different admissions criteria

laws.title: SB 4: State Immigration Enforcement
laws.subtitle: Texas's controversial self-deportation and state arrest law
laws.fullDescription: Texas's SB 4 (2024) created a new state crime for illegal entry into Texas from a foreign nation and authorized state police to arrest migrants who crossed the border illegally, with judges able to order them to return to Mexico. This represented an unprecedented expansion of state immigration enforcement powers traditionally held by the federal government. The law was immediately challenged by the Biden administration. The Supreme Court allowed SB 4 to take effect while litigation continued. Critics argue only the federal government has immigration enforcement authority under the Constitution.
laws.penalty: Illegal entry into Texas under SB 4 is a Class B misdemeanor (up to 180 days jail); repeat entry is a felony; judges may order violators to return to Mexico rather than face incarceration
exceptions: Law does not apply to lawful permanent residents or visa holders
Federal immigration processes and asylum claims remain under federal jurisdiction
laws.sourceLabel: Texas SB 4 (2024) – Illegal Entry State Crime

quiz.q: Texas SB 4 (2024) was unprecedented because it created a state law criminalizing what traditionally federal jurisdiction?
options: Illegal border crossing (state crime for federal immigration violation)
quiz.explanation: SB 4 created a state criminal offense for crossing the Texas border illegally, an area traditionally governed exclusively by federal law. This was constitutionally controversial because immigration enforcement is generally a federal power under the Supremacy Clause.

laws.title: Strict Drug Laws and Death Penalty
laws.subtitle: Texas's severe drug penalties and capital punishment for trafficking
laws.fullDescription: Texas maintains some of the nation's harshest drug laws. Texas law allows the death penalty for certain large-scale drug trafficking convictions (though rarely pursued). Possession of even small amounts of controlled substances can result in felony charges. Texas is one of the few states that classifies marijuana possession of any amount as a criminal offense (misdemeanor for small amounts, felony for over 4 oz). Texas leads the nation in drug-related incarcerations. Harris County (Houston) and Dallas County have implemented limited non-prosecution policies for small cannabis amounts.
laws.penalty: Marijuana possession under 2 oz: Class B misdemeanor (180 days jail/$2,000 fine); over 4 lbs: felony; cocaine possession: felony from 180 days to life; delivery of drugs causing death: up to life imprisonment; large-scale trafficking: up to 99 years
exceptions: Compassionate Use Program allows limited medical cannabis (low-THC) for specific conditions
Some counties have adopted cite-and-release policies for small marijuana amounts
laws.sourceLabel: Texas Health and Safety Code – Controlled Substances

quiz.q: What makes Texas's drug trafficking law potentially unique among US states?
options: It bans drug testing at work
It allows the death penalty for certain large-scale trafficking convictions
It requires mandatory treatment for first-time offenders
It classifies all drug possession as civil violations
quiz.explanation: Texas law technically permits the death penalty for certain large-scale drug trafficking offenses (delivery of controlled substances causing death and related provisions), though this is rarely pursued. Texas also has extremely severe mandatory minimum sentences for drug trafficking.

laws.title: Texas LGBTQ+ Restrictions
laws.subtitle: Texas's anti-LGBTQ+ legislation wave
laws.fullDescription: Texas has enacted some of the most restrictive LGBTQ+ laws in the US. SB 14 (2023) bans gender-affirming care (puberty blockers, hormone therapy) for minors. Texas law prevents transgender students from using bathrooms matching their gender identity in public schools. Texas attempted to require social workers to report families of transgender children to Child Protective Services. The Texas Attorney General sent letters to LGBTQ+ book publishers. No state-level LGBTQ+ non-discrimination protections exist, though some cities (Austin, Dallas, Houston) have local ordinances.
laws.penalty: Healthcare providers performing gender-affirming care on minors: civil liability, license revocation; violation of bathroom policies in schools: administrative sanctions; no criminal penalties for being LGBTQ+, but local non-discrimination enforcement is weak without state backing
exceptions: SB 14 exempts individuals who started treatment before September 2023 (transition period)
Federal employment protections (Bostock) apply regardless of state law
Some Texas cities maintain local LGBTQ+ non-discrimination ordinances
laws.sourceLabel: Texas SB 14 (2023) and LGBTQ+ Policy Framework

quiz.q: Texas's SB 14 (2023) banned which medical treatments for transgender minors?
options: All medical treatment related to gender identity
quiz.explanation: Texas SB 14 bans puberty blockers (GnRH agonists) and cross-sex hormone therapy for minors with gender dysphoria, forcing families to either move to states where treatment is available or cease ongoing treatment.

laws.title: Limited Shield Law — Press Freedom Under Pressure
laws.subtitle: Texas has a moderate shield law but media ownership concentration raises concerns
laws.fullDescription: Texas has a reporter's privilege under the Texas Free Flow of Information Act (2009), which protects journalists from disclosing confidential sources or unpublished information, with exceptions for criminal proceedings where the information is essential. Texas also has anti-SLAPP protections under the Texas Citizens Participation Act (TCPA). However, media ownership in Texas is heavily concentrated among large corporations. Texas public officials have been vocal critics of press coverage, and the state legislature has considered bills that could affect press operations. The Texas Tribune and Houston Chronicle are prominent outlets.
laws.penalty: Journalists may be compelled to testify in criminal proceedings under specific conditions; TCPA provides anti-SLAPP protection
exceptions: Criminal cases where the information is essential and not otherwise obtainable

quiz.q: What exceptions exist to Texas's reporter shield law for journalists?
options: Criminal proceedings where information is essential and unavailable elsewhere
quiz.explanation: Texas's Free Flow of Information Act protects journalists from source disclosure but has an exception for criminal proceedings where the information is essential to the case and cannot be obtained elsewhere — a significant carve-out compared to California's absolute privilege.

laws.title: HB 20 — Anti-Censorship Law for Social Media Platforms
laws.subtitle: Texas's HB 20 prohibits large social media platforms from censoring users based on viewpoint
laws.fullDescription: Texas passed HB 20 (2021), which prohibits large social media platforms (over 50 million US monthly active users) from censoring users based on political viewpoint. The law was challenged by tech industry groups. The US Supreme Court in Moody v. NetChoice (2024) remanded First Amendment challenges, leaving the law's constitutionality unsettled. Texas has also passed data privacy legislation and children's online safety laws. Texas reflects a conservative approach to social media regulation focusing on platform neutrality rather than user data protection.
laws.penalty: Texas AG can seek injunctions against platforms that violate HB 20's anti-censorship provisions
exceptions: First Amendment challenge remanded by Supreme Court; constitutionality remains unsettled

quiz.q: What does Texas's HB 20 prohibit large social media platforms from doing?
options: Censoring users based on political viewpoint
quiz.explanation: Texas's HB 20 prohibits large social media platforms from censoring users based on political viewpoint — a law driven by conservative concerns about perceived anti-conservative bias on platforms like Twitter/X and Facebook, though its constitutionality under the First Amendment remains contested.

laws.title: Texas Banking and Crypto Mining Hub
laws.subtitle: Texas is a major crypto mining center with relatively favorable banking regulations
laws.fullDescription: Texas has become a major hub for cryptocurrency mining due to cheap energy (particularly wind) and favorable regulatory stance. The Texas Department of Banking has issued guidance recognizing cryptocurrency as legitimate business for banks to engage with. Texas's Finance Commission oversees banking regulation. Texas has no state income tax, making it attractive for financial services. The Texas crypto mining industry attracted operations after China's 2021 mining ban. Texas has community banking traditions and large credit union networks. The Texas Securities Board regulates crypto-related securities.
laws.penalty: Texas banking violations subject to state regulatory action; securities violations subject to TSB enforcement
exceptions: Federal banking regulations take precedence for nationally chartered institutions

quiz.q: Why did Texas become a major cryptocurrency mining hub, especially after 2021?
options: Texas passed a crypto mining subsidy law
Texas has cheap energy (wind) and favorable regulation; China banned mining in 2021
Texas offered tax exemptions for mining
quiz.explanation: Texas became a major crypto mining hub due to cheap electricity from its large wind energy sector, favorable state regulatory stance, and the exodus of mining operations from China following China's 2021 cryptocurrency mining ban — making Texas the largest US state for crypto mining by capacity.

laws.title: Texas Cottage Food Law & DSHS Food Safety Regulations
laws.subtitle: Texas has one of the US's most permissive cottage food laws alongside standard commercial safety rules
laws.fullDescription: Texas has one of America's most permissive cottage food laws, allowing home bakers and food producers to sell directly to consumers without a commercial kitchen or food facility license — with annual sales up to $50,000 and for non-potentially-hazardous foods. The Texas Department of State Health Services (DSHS) and Texas Department of Agriculture (TDA) regulate food safety for commercial producers. Texas's 'Cottage Food Producer' can sell at farmers markets, roadside stands, or directly to consumers. However, cottage food cannot be sold online for shipping or to retailers. Texas also regulates meat processing facilities separately under the Texas Department of Agriculture, with state-inspected facilities allowed to sell only within Texas.
laws.penalty: Commercial food safety violations: DSHS can issue cease and desist, fines vary by violation; cottage food violations (retail/shipping): misdemeanor charges; adulterated food distribution: up to $10,000 fine and 1 year imprisonment
exceptions: True cottage food producers (below thresholds, non-hazardous foods) need no license
Agricultural fairs and private events have modified rules
USDA-federally inspected meat can be sold interstate; state-inspected only within Texas

quiz.q: What is the maximum annual sales limit for a Texas Cottage Food Producer selling home-made foods directly to consumers?
quiz.explanation: Texas's Cottage Food Law allows home food producers to sell directly to consumers up to $50,000 annually without a commercial kitchen license — one of America's more generous limits, reflecting Texas's generally business-friendly regulatory philosophy.

laws.title: Texas Animal Cruelty Laws — Loco's Law
laws.subtitle: Felony protections for pets; livestock exemptions broad
laws.fullDescription: Texas Penal Code Section 42.09 and 42.092 govern animal cruelty. Section 42.092 ('Loco's Law', named after a mutilated dog) elevated intentional animal cruelty from a misdemeanor to a felony in 2001 — a landmark change. Torturing, killing, poisoning, or seriously injuring a non-livestock animal is a state jail felony (2nd or 3rd degree for repeat offenses). Texas also has animal fighting laws (cockfighting and dogfighting are felonies). However, Texas has broad agricultural exemptions — standard farm practices like branding, dehorning, and castration are explicitly excluded from cruelty laws.
laws.penalty: State jail felony: 180 days–2 years + up to $10,000 fine; 3rd degree felony for repeat: 2–10 years; attending dogfight: Class A misdemeanor
exceptions: Livestock and equine animal practices — branding, dehorning, castration
Hunting, fishing, and trapping under state license
Scientific research under USDA IACUC oversight

quiz.q: What was the significance of Texas's 'Loco's Law' passed in 2001?
options: It created the first Texas animal shelter system
It elevated intentional animal cruelty from misdemeanor to felony
It required microchipping for all pets
quiz.explanation: Loco's Law (named after a dog that was mutilated) elevated intentional cruelty to non-livestock animals from a misdemeanor to a felony in Texas — a landmark 2001 reform that inspired similar laws in other states.

laws.title: Texas Community Property and Divorce Law
laws.subtitle: Texas is a community property state with a 60-day divorce waiting period
laws.fullDescription: Texas is a community property state — assets acquired during marriage are presumed equally owned. Texas has a 60-day mandatory waiting period after filing for divorce before it can be finalized. Contested divorces can take significantly longer. Texas courts apply 'just and right' division of community property, which can but need not be exactly 50/50. Texas has unique 'covenant marriage' law allowing couples to opt into harder-to-dissolve marriages. Child custody ('conservatorship' in Texas) focuses on the best interests of the child, with a presumption in favor of joint managing conservatorship. Texas has no common-law marriage by default but does recognize informal marriages with elements of agreement, cohabitation, and holding out as married.
laws.penalty: Civil family law enforcement; contempt: fines and possible jail for violating orders; child support non-compliance: licence suspension, passport denial, criminal non-support charges
exceptions: Separate property (pre-marital, gifts, inheritance)
Premarital agreements
Covenant marriage has stricter divorce requirements

quiz.q: What unique marriage option does Texas offer that makes divorce harder to obtain?
options: Covenant marriage — couples opt into stricter grounds required for divorce
Sacred bond marriage recognized by courts
quiz.explanation: Texas (along with Louisiana and Arizona) allows 'covenant marriage' — couples who choose this option agree to premarital counseling and can only divorce on specific grounds like adultery, felony conviction, abuse, or after a 2-year separation. It's a conservative religious alternative to standard marriage with easier divorce.

laws.title: Texas Property Rights & Eminent Domain Reform
laws.subtitle: Strong private property protections with landowner rights
laws.fullDescription: Texas has some of the strongest eminent domain protections in the U.S. following HB 1495 (2011) and SB 421 (2021). Property owners must receive at least three written offers before condemnation proceedings, and the Texas Landowner's Bill of Rights guarantees compensation for diminished access. Proposition 2 (2009) also strengthened protections against regulatory takings. Texas does not have rent control, with state law preempting local rent control ordinances.
laws.penalty: Property owners entitled to 'adequate compensation'; litigation costs recoverable if award exceeds final offer by 20%+
exceptions: Bona fide public use required
No residential rent control statewide

quiz.q: What does Texas law require before condemnation proceedings can begin against a property owner?
quiz.explanation: Texas HB 1495 requires condemning entities to make at least three written offers to property owners before condemnation proceedings can begin, ensuring owners have multiple opportunities to negotiate.

laws.title: Texas Deceptive Trade Practices Act (DTPA)
laws.subtitle: Triple damages for knowing deceptive trade practices
laws.fullDescription: Texas's Deceptive Trade Practices-Consumer Protection Act (DTPA, Bus. & Comm. Code Ch. 17) is one of the nation's strongest consumer protection statutes. It prohibits false, misleading, or deceptive acts in trade or commerce. Consumers can recover actual damages, mental anguish damages, and if the defendant acted 'knowingly,' up to three times economic damages. If intentionally fraudulent, courts can award up to three times total damages. The DTPA covers goods, services, and real estate. Consumers must send a 60-day demand letter before filing suit. The Texas AG can also sue for injunctions and civil penalties up to $20,000 per violation.
laws.penalty: Knowing violation: up to 3x economic damages; intentional violation: up to 3x total damages; AG penalties: up to $20,000 per violation
exceptions: 60-day pre-suit demand letter required from consumer
Covers goods, services, and real estate transactions

quiz.q: What maximum multiplier can Texas courts apply to economic damages for a 'knowing' DTPA violation?
quiz.explanation: Texas's DTPA allows courts to award up to three times economic damages when a defendant acted 'knowingly' in committing a deceptive trade practice — a powerful deterrent since even modest underlying damages can result in large multiplied awards.

laws.title: Constitutional Carry — No Permit Required
laws.subtitle: HB 1927 (2021) — Permitless carry for eligible Texans
laws.fullDescription: Texas passed permitless carry in 2021, allowing Texans 21+ who are not prohibited by law from possessing firearms to carry a handgun openly or concealed without a license. A License to Carry (LTC) is still available for reciprocity in other states.
laws.penalty: Carrying while prohibited (felons, domestic abusers): state jail felony to 3rd degree felony.
exceptions: Felons and those with domestic violence convictions remain prohibited
Schools, polling places, courts remain gun-free zones
Intoxicated persons may not carry

quiz.q: What is the minimum age for permitless carry in Texas?
quiz.explanation: Texas permitless carry (HB 1927) applies to Texans aged 21 and over who are legally eligible to possess a firearm.

laws.title: Texting While Driving Ban
laws.subtitle: Texas Transportation Code §545.4251 — $99–$200 fine
laws.fullDescription: Texas banned texting while driving statewide in 2017. Drivers may not read, write, or send electronic messages while driving. The ban applies even at red lights. Hands-free calls are permitted.
laws.penalty: $99 first offense, up to $200 subsequent.
exceptions: Hands-free calling permitted if activated before driving
Emergency calls to 911 permitted
Navigation apps allowed if pre-programmed

quiz.q: Is texting at a red light legal in Texas?
options: No, it is illegal at all times while driving
quiz.explanation: Texas's texting ban applies even when stopped at red lights — the vehicle must be off the road entirely for texting to be legal.

laws.title: Castle Doctrine & Stand Your Ground
laws.subtitle: Texas Penal Code §9.31–9.32 — No duty to retreat
laws.fullDescription: Texas has one of the nation's strongest castle doctrines. There is no duty to retreat anywhere you have a legal right to be. Deadly force is justified to protect yourself or others from death, serious injury, kidnapping, or to prevent robbery, arson, or burglary of your vehicle.
laws.penalty: N/A — This is a legal defense. Improper use of deadly force results in murder or manslaughter charges.
exceptions: Cannot be the initial aggressor
Cannot invoke if engaged in criminal activity
Must have a legal right to be in the location

quiz.q: Does Texas have a duty to retreat before using deadly force?
options: No, Texas has no duty to retreat
quiz.explanation: Texas has no duty to retreat — you may stand your ground anywhere you have a legal right to be, including public spaces.

laws.title: No State Income Tax
laws.subtitle: Texas Constitution Article 8 — Zero personal income tax
laws.fullDescription: Texas has no state income tax, enshrined in the Texas Constitution. Voters approved Prop 4 in 2019 making it harder to enact one. Texas funds government via sales tax (up to 8.25%), property tax, and oil/gas severance taxes. Property taxes are among the nation's highest.
laws.penalty: N/A — This is a tax absence, not a law with penalties.
exceptions: Federal income tax still applies
Businesses pay franchise tax (margin tax)
Sales tax applies to most goods and services

quiz.q: How does Texas primarily fund state government without income tax?
quiz.explanation: Texas relies heavily on sales tax (up to 8.25%) and property taxes — which are among the highest in the US — to fund state and local government.

laws.title: Blue Laws — Sunday Liquor Store Closure
laws.subtitle: Texas Alcoholic Beverage Code — Regulated hours
laws.fullDescription: Texas has complex alcohol sale rules. Liquor stores (package stores) cannot sell on Sundays. Beer and wine can be sold at grocery and convenience stores Sunday 10am–midnight. Bars can open at 10am on Sundays. Sales generally end at midnight weekdays and 1am Friday-Saturday.
laws.penalty: Fines, license suspension, or revocation for ABC violations.
exceptions: Restaurants with mixed beverage permits may serve on Sundays
Hotels have different rules
Local option elections can change some rules

quiz.q: Can liquor stores in Texas sell alcohol on Sundays?
options: No, liquor stores cannot sell on Sundays
quiz.explanation: Texas liquor (package) stores are prohibited from selling on Sundays — a blue law holdover. Beer and wine at grocery stores are allowed Sunday 10am–midnight.

laws.title: Post-Dobbs Near-Total Abortion Ban
laws.subtitle: Texas HB 1280 — Trigger law, 2022
laws.fullDescription: After Dobbs (2022), Texas's trigger law (HB 1280) took effect, banning virtually all abortions with narrow medical exceptions. Earlier, SB 8 (2021) banned abortion after ~6 weeks with private civil enforcement. Private citizens can sue abortion providers for $10,000+ per violation.
laws.penalty: Criminal: life imprisonment or up to 99 years. Civil: $10,000+ per procedure.
exceptions: Life-threatening medical emergency
Limited exceptions for ectopic pregnancy, sepsis
No exception for rape or incest under trigger law

quiz.q: Who enforces Texas's SB 8 abortion law?
quiz.explanation: SB 8 deputizes private citizens to sue anyone who aids or abets an abortion after 6 weeks for at least $10,000 ��� a unique civil enforcement mechanism.

laws.title: Annual Vehicle Safety Inspection Requirement
laws.subtitle: Texas Transportation Code — Annual inspection
laws.fullDescription: Texas requires annual vehicle safety inspections at licensed stations checking brakes, lights, tires, horn, wipers, and mirrors. In major metro areas, emissions testing is included. Cost is $7 state fee plus station charges. Out-of-state vehicles must inspect within 90 days of becoming a Texas resident.
laws.penalty: $12.50 citation for expired inspection sticker.
exceptions: Vehicles 25+ years old exempt from emissions testing
Motorcycles exempt from emissions test
Military vehicles on deployment get extended grace periods

quiz.q: How often must most Texas vehicles pass a safety inspection?
quiz.explanation: Texas requires annual vehicle safety inspections. Major metro counties also include emissions testing as part of the inspection.

laws.title: Home Schooling — Minimal State Regulation
laws.subtitle: Texas Education Code — Parent-directed education rights
laws.fullDescription: Texas has some of the most relaxed homeschool laws in the US. Families do not need to register with the state, notify the school district, or have children tested. The curriculum must include reading, spelling, grammar, math, and good citizenship. Home-schooled children are treated as attending private school.
laws.penalty: Fraudulent enrollment using false address: class C misdemeanor.
exceptions: Curriculum must cover basic subjects
No state registration or testing required
College admissions tests available without restrictions

quiz.q: Must Texas homeschooling families register with the state?
options: No, no registration or testing required
quiz.explanation: Texas has some of the most relaxed homeschool laws in the US — families do not need to register with the state, notify the district, or have children tested.

laws.title: Homestead Exemption — $100,000 (2023)
laws.subtitle: Texas Tax Code §11.13 — Voter-approved increase
laws.fullDescription: Texas offers a $100,000 homestead exemption reducing the taxable value of primary residences for school district taxes, after voters approved an increase from $40,000 in 2023. Seniors (65+) get an additional $10,000. Property taxes still remain high despite exemptions.
laws.penalty: Fraudulent homestead exemption claim: fine up to $5,000 plus repayment of taxes avoided.
exceptions: Only primary residence qualifies
Must be Texas resident
Agricultural land uses ag exemption

quiz.q: What is Texas's homestead exemption for school district taxes as of 2023?
quiz.explanation: Texas voters approved a constitutional amendment in 2023 raising the homestead exemption for school district taxes from $40,000 to $100,000, providing significant property tax relief.

laws.title: ERCOT Grid — Deregulated Electricity Market
laws.subtitle: Texas Electric Reliability Council — Independent grid
laws.fullDescription: Texas operates its own electric grid (ERCOT), largely independent from the national grid, with a deregulated retail market. Customers in most areas choose their electricity provider. The February 2021 winter storm (Uri) caused catastrophic grid failure, killing hundreds. Reform legislation (SB 3) required weatherization.
laws.penalty: Utilities failing weatherization requirements: PUCT fines up to $1 million per violation per day.
exceptions: Some co-ops and municipal utilities remain regulated
West Texas connects to other grids
Transmission remains regulated

quiz.q: What makes Texas's electric grid unique among US states?
options: It is mostly independent from the national US grid
quiz.explanation: ERCOT operates largely independently of the Eastern and Western Interconnections, giving Texas its own electric grid and keeping federal regulation minimal.

laws.title: Drug-Free Zone Enhanced Penalties
laws.subtitle: Texas Health & Safety Code §481.134 — Doubled sentences
laws.fullDescription: Drug offenses committed within 1,000 feet of a school, playground, video arcade, or youth center carry doubled minimum sentences in Texas. This applies to possession, delivery, and manufacture. The enhanced zone also covers university campuses and public pools.
laws.penalty: Mandatory doubled minimums — e.g., delivery of cocaine becomes minimum 10 years near a school.
exceptions: Enhancement requires proof of knowing proximity to school
Defense may argue lack of knowledge
Some courts look at whether the zone actively attracted youth

quiz.q: By how much are drug offense penalties enhanced in Texas school zones?
quiz.explanation: Texas doubles the minimum sentence for drug offenses within 1,000 feet of a school, playground, or youth center under the drug-free zone enhancement.

laws.title: Water Rights — Prior Appropriation & Rule of Capture
laws.subtitle: Texas Water Code — Split surface and groundwater rules
laws.fullDescription: Texas surface water follows prior appropriation administered by TCEQ. Groundwater is different — Texas recognizes the Rule of Capture allowing landowners to pump as much groundwater as they want from beneath their property. Groundwater districts may regulate but property rights are strong.
laws.penalty: Surface water without permit: TCEQ fines up to $25,000/day.
exceptions: Domestic use exemptions for small quantities
Livestock watering exemptions
Some groundwater districts impose production limits

quiz.q: Under Texas's Rule of Capture, who owns the groundwater beneath private land?
options: The landowner can pump as much as they want
quiz.explanation: Texas's Rule of Capture allows landowners to pump groundwater beneath their property without limit, unlike most states. Groundwater districts may impose some regulations.

laws.title: Voter ID Law — Photo ID Required
laws.subtitle: Texas Election Code §63.0101 — Strict photo ID
laws.fullDescription: Texas requires voters to show approved photo ID at polling places. Accepted IDs include Texas DL, state ID, passport, military ID, or handgun license. Voters lacking photo ID may sign an affidavit and show supporting ID. Texas has strict enforcement.
laws.penalty: Voting fraud: state jail felony (180 days–2 years). Illegal voting: 2nd degree felony.
exceptions: Voters 70+ with consistent registration may qualify for exemption
Voters with disability may use supporting documentation
Mail ballots have signature verification
laws.sourceLabel: Texas Secretary of State — Voter ID

quiz.q: Is a Texas handgun license an acceptable voter ID in Texas?
quiz.explanation: A Texas License to Carry (handgun license) is an approved photo ID for voting, along with driver's licenses, state IDs, passports, and military IDs.

laws.title: Death Penalty — Most Executions in the US
laws.subtitle: Texas Code of Criminal Procedure — Lethal injection
laws.fullDescription: Texas executes more prisoners than any other US state, accounting for roughly 1/3 of all US executions. Death penalty applies to capital murder with aggravating factors. Lethal injection is the method used.
laws.penalty: Death by lethal injection with automatic appeal through the Court of Criminal Appeals.
exceptions: Intellectual disability: Atkins v. Virginia prohibits execution
Juveniles: Roper v. Simmons prohibits execution for crimes committed under 18
No categorical mental illness exemption in Texas

quiz.q: Approximately what fraction of US executions does Texas perform?
quiz.explanation: Texas has historically carried out approximately one-third of all executions in the United States — more than any other state.

laws.title: Right to Farm — Agricultural Operations Protected
laws.subtitle: Texas Agriculture Code — Nuisance lawsuit protection
laws.fullDescription: Texas has strong right-to-farm laws protecting agricultural operations from nuisance lawsuits. Farming, ranching, wildlife management, and timber operations legally established before neighboring development are largely protected. Agricultural land gets the ag exemption dramatically reducing property taxes.
laws.penalty: Fraudulent ag exemption claims: back taxes plus 5% interest and penalties.
exceptions: Operations that significantly expand may lose protection
Violations of state law not protected
Certain pollution activities not covered

quiz.q: What tax benefit does agricultural land receive in Texas?
options: Ag exemption — taxed on productive value, not market value
quiz.explanation: Texas agricultural land is taxed based on its agricultural productive value, not market value — dramatically reducing property taxes for farmers and ranchers.

laws.title: 85 mph Speed Limit — Highest in the US
laws.subtitle: Texas Transportation Code — Variable limits by road
laws.fullDescription: Texas has the highest posted speed limit in the US — 85 mph on SH 130 (toll road between Austin and San Antonio). Most rural interstates are 75–80 mph. Urban interstates typically 60–70 mph.
laws.penalty: Speeding: $97–$200 base fine plus court costs.
exceptions: Emergency vehicles exempt when responding
Advisory speed limits on curves
Commercial vehicles may have lower limits

quiz.q: What is the highest legal speed limit in Texas?
quiz.explanation: SH 130 has an 85 mph speed limit — the highest posted speed limit in the United States.

laws.title: Open Beaches Act — Public Gulf Coast Access
laws.subtitle: Texas Natural Resources Code §61 — Guaranteed access
laws.fullDescription: The Texas Open Beaches Act guarantees public access to all Gulf Coast beaches to the mean high tide line. Private landowners cannot block beach access even if they own property behind the dunes. The public easement moves with the vegetation line.
laws.penalty: Blocking beach access: civil enforcement, fines, and mandatory removal of barriers.
exceptions: Private piers may have limited access restrictions
Endangered species nesting areas may have temporary closures
Military installations restrict access

quiz.q: Who has the right to access Gulf Coast beaches under the Texas Open Beaches Act?
options: The general public, guaranteed by law
quiz.explanation: Texas's Open Beaches Act guarantees the public the right to access all Gulf Coast beaches up to the vegetation line, regardless of adjacent private land ownership.

laws.title: Oil & Gas Royalty — Mineral Rights Dominate
laws.subtitle: Texas common law — Mineral estate dominance
laws.fullDescription: In Texas, mineral rights (oil, gas) can be severed from surface rights. The mineral estate is legally 'dominant' — mineral rights holders can access the surface for drilling with limited liability. Surface owners receive damages but cannot prevent drilling. Texas has no forced pooling.
laws.penalty: Unauthorized drilling: trespass liability. Mineral rights theft: criminal penalties.
exceptions: Surface damage agreements often negotiated
Railroad Commission regulates drilling operations
Eminent domain may apply to pipeline routes

quiz.q: Which estate is 'dominant' when mineral and surface rights are separated in Texas?
options: Mineral estate — mineral rights holders have priority
quiz.explanation: In Texas, the mineral estate is legally 'dominant' — mineral rights owners can access land for drilling even over surface owners' objections, with compensation for damages.

laws.title: Same-Sex Marriage — Obergefell Applies
laws.subtitle: Obergefell v. Hodges (2015) — Federal requirement
laws.fullDescription: Following the US Supreme Court's Obergefell decision (2015), same-sex marriage is legal in Texas. State agencies, counties, and municipalities must recognize same-sex marriages. The 2022 Respect for Marriage Act federally codified same-sex marriage protections. Some Texas county clerks initially resisted but compliance is required.
laws.penalty: County clerks refusing to issue licenses: civil rights lawsuits, removal from office.
exceptions: Religious organizations retain rights to decline performing ceremonies
Private businesses with sincere religious beliefs have some protection
Individual clerks may deputize others to issue licenses

quiz.q: Is same-sex marriage legally recognized in Texas?
quiz.explanation: Same-sex marriage is fully legal in Texas following Obergefell v. Hodges (2015) and reinforced by the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act.

laws.title: Marijuana — Class B Misdemeanor Under 2oz
laws.subtitle: Texas Health & Safety Code §481.121 — Still illegal statewide
laws.fullDescription: Marijuana is illegal in Texas statewide. Possession of under 2oz is a Class B misdemeanor (up to 180 days/$2,000). Austin, Dallas, and several cities have decriminalized small amounts for local enforcement. State police can still enforce. Medical CBD oil legal for limited conditions.
laws.penalty: Under 2oz: Class B misdemeanor, up to 180 days, $2,000 fine. Over 4oz: felony.
exceptions: Medical CBD (low-THC) oil legal under Compassionate Use Program
Hemp with <0.3% THC is legal
Some cities have decriminalized small amounts

quiz.q: What is the maximum penalty for possessing under 2 oz of marijuana in Texas?
options: Up to 180 days jail and $2,000 fine
quiz.explanation: Possession of less than 2 oz of marijuana in Texas is a Class B misdemeanor, punishable by up to 180 days in jail and a $2,000 fine.
